seems: gives the impression of being something
It seems likely that prices will keep rising this year.
very: used to make an adjective or adverb stronger
The soup tasted very good after such a cold walk.
making: Making bread from scratch takes patience and practice.
means: A nod usually means agreement in most cultures.
should: used to say what is correct, expected, or advisable
You should see a doctor if the pain continues for another week.
ignored: paid no attention to something deliberately, past tense
Her advice was ignored until it was too late.
wars: periods of armed fighting between countries or groups
Before refrigeration, salt decided which wars a country could afford.
pandemics: disease outbreaks occurring across wide areas or worldwide
Historians have studied how past pandemics reshaped entire societies.
climate: the general weather conditions typical of an area over a long period
The region has a mild climate with cool, wet winters.
change: A single ingredient can change the whole flavour of a dish.
real: actually existing; genuine, not imagined or fake
The documentary tells the real story behind the famous painting.
demand: to require or need something firmly
Modern customers demand fast and reliable delivery service.
society: a large community of people living together in an organized way
Education plays a key role in shaping a fair society.
heard: perceived sound with the ears; past tense of hear
She heard footsteps approaching from behind the door.
only: and no one or nothing more besides; just
Only a handful of tickets remained by the time we arrived.
would: used to express a hypothetical or past future action
Fifty years ago, people asked which jobs machines would take first.
dangerously: in a way that is likely to cause harm or loss
The car was travelling dangerously close to the edge of the cliff.
uninformed: lacking knowledge or information about something
A society that heard only pleasant stories would be dangerously uninformed.
press: She had to press the dough firmly before placing it in the oven.
exposes: reveals something hidden, or leaves something uncovered
A press that exposes wrongdoing does genuinely valuable work.
wrongdoing: A press that exposes wrongdoing does valuable work for society.
does: performs an action, or auxiliary form used in questions and negatives
She does her best to help everyone around her.
valuable: worth a lot of money or very useful
Her advice proved valuable when we were planning the trip.
work: activity involving effort, especially to earn a living or achieve something
The difference is not impatience on one side; it is what is doing the work.
trouble: difficulty, problems, or a source of worry
The trouble starts when its clock and the world's disagree.
arises: comes into existence or becomes apparent
A problem arises whenever two departments interpret the same rule differently.
constant: happening all the time or not changing
The factory produces a constant hum that neighbours have complained about.
flow: the steady, continuous movement of something, such as liquid
Engineers measured the flow of the river after the storm.
alarm: a warning sound or signal indicating danger
The fire alarm went off just as the meeting was ending.
leaves: goes away from a place, or allows something to remain (he/she/it)
The train leaves the station every hour on the hour.
better: of higher quality or more suitable than something else
The second recipe turned out much better than the first attempt.
informed: having enough knowledge or facts to understand a situation well
được thông tin đầy đủ, am hiểu
Voters need accurate news to make informed choices at elections.
simply: in an easy or straightforward way; just, merely
She simply smiled and walked away without saying a word.
helpless: unable to protect or help oneself
bất lực, không thể làm gì
She felt helpless watching the flood rise around the house.
consequences: results or effects of actions or conditions
Ignoring the warning signs had serious consequences for the whole team.
who: used to ask about or refer to a person
The extra heat is dangerous for anyone who cannot afford to cool their home.
overwhelmed: given more of something than one can deal with; completely overcome
She felt overwhelmed by the number of messages waiting for her.
may: The meeting may be postponed if too few people attend.
stop: to come to an end or cause something to end
The bus will stop right outside the school gate.
following: coming next in time or order
They planned to travel again the following spring.
altogether: The old bridge was closed altogether after the inspection found serious cracks.
rather: She chose to walk rather than take the crowded bus.
others: other people or things not already mentioned
Some students finished early, while others needed the full hour.
become: It can take years of practice to become a skilled musician.
convinced: certain about something after being persuaded
After reading the report, she was convinced the plan would work.
affect: to have an influence on or produce a change in something
Lack of sleep can seriously affect a person's concentration.
vote: to formally choose between options, such as in an election
People planned to vote for the candidate who promised lower taxes.
let: to allow someone to do something
Her parents let her stay out late for the concert.
their: belonging to or associated with the people or things just mentioned
The students left their bags in the classroom overnight.
children: plural of child; young human beings
The park was full of children playing after school.
play: to spend time doing enjoyable activities, especially as children do
Children love to play outside after school ends.
trust: firm belief in the reliability or honesty of someone or something
The conditions that make local management work include a group small enough to know one another and trust each other.
strangers: She never talks to strangers on the train.
anxiety: a feeling of worry or nervousness about something
Public speaking causes a lot of anxiety for many students.
poor: not good in quality, ability, or amount; weak
The bridge was closed after inspectors found its poor condition dangerous.
lens: a curved piece of glass used to focus light, or a way of viewing something
Through this lens, the decision looks far more reasonable.
judging: forming an opinion about something based on evidence
Judging by the dark clouds, it will probably rain soon.
risk: the possibility of something bad or dangerous happening
Investing in a new business always carries some risk.
pattern: a regular, repeated way in which something happens or is arranged
Analysts noticed a clear pattern in the company's sales figures.
familiar: The song sounded familiar, though she couldn't remember its name.
southeast: the direction or region midway between south and east
They spent a month backpacking around Southeast Asia.
asia: the largest continent, covering much of the eastern hemisphere
The company plans to expand its business across Southeast Asia next year.
now: at the present time; at this moment
Now is a good time to start saving for retirement.
get: to obtain, receive, or come to have something
He hopes to get a promotion later this year.
messaging: the sending of messages, especially electronically
The two teams stay in touch through a shared messaging app.
apps: computer programs, especially for mobile devices
Many students use language-learning apps to practise a few minutes daily.
newspapers: printed publications containing news, issued regularly
Old newspapers filled the boxes stacked in the attic.
television: a device that receives broadcast signals and shows moving pictures with sound
The family gathered around the television to watch the final match.
dramatic: sudden and striking; exciting or impressive
The city saw a dramatic rise in temperature this summer.
videos: recordings of moving images, often with sound
Dramatic videos of the storm spread quickly online.
road: a wide path with a hard surface for vehicles
A new road now connects the two remote villages.
accidents: unplanned or unfortunate events, often causing injury or damage
The new traffic lights reduced accidents at the busy junction.
floods: overflows of water onto normally dry land
Seasonal floods once enriched the soil along the river banks.
quarrels: Family quarrels over money can sometimes last for years.
street: a public road in a town or city, usually lined with buildings
Children were playing football in the street after school.
circulate: to spread or move around among a group of people
Rumours about the merger began to circulate around the office.
stripped: having had a covering or parts removed
The old car was found stripped of its wheels and engine.
context: the circumstances or setting in which something happens
Without more context, the quote could easily be misunderstood.
reporter: a person who writes or presents news stories
A young reporter interviewed the mayor after the ceremony.
add: to put something together with something else to increase it
Please add a pinch of salt before serving the soup.
retired: having left one's job, especially due to age
đã về hưu, ngừng sử dụng
Her retired parents now spend their days gardening.
teacher: a person whose job is to teach
Her favourite teacher always made history lessons feel like stories.
provincial: relating to a province or a region outside the capital
The provincial government announced new funding for rural hospitals.
town: a populated area smaller than a city, with houses and shops
Picture a sunny afternoon in a desert town.
spends: uses time or money on something
She spends most weekends hiking in the mountains.
her: belonging to a female previously mentioned
She left her umbrella on the train this morning.
evenings: the parts of the day between afternoon and night
She spends her evenings forwarding videos to family group chats.
forwarding: sending something, such as a message, on to another person or place
She keeps forwarding funny videos to her family group chat.
clips: plural of clip; short extracts from a film or video
He spends hours scrolling through short video clips every evening.
family: a group of related people, or a group of related things
This plant belongs to the same family as the rose.
groups: put people or things into sets sharing a characteristic
The teacher groups the students by ability before each project.
out: away from the inside of a place; not in
She stepped out for a few minutes to get some fresh air.
genuine: real and authentic; not fake or pretended
Her smile showed genuine happiness at the news.
concern: a feeling of worry, or a matter of interest or importance
Rising prices have become a major concern for many families.
intentions: plans or aims that guide someone's actions
His intentions were good, even though the plan eventually failed.
kind: a type or category of something
This kind of bread takes several hours to rise properly.
combined: joined together to form a single whole
Their combined efforts finished the project two weeks early.
effect: a change that results from an action or cause
Cutting sugar had a noticeable effect on her energy levels.
relatives: Dozens of relatives gathered for the wedding celebration last weekend.
steady: not changing, moving or shaking; firm and regular
He kept a steady pace throughout the marathon.
background: the part of a scene or situation that is behind or supports the main part
Mountains formed a striking background in every photo they took.
hum: tiếng vo ve, tiếng ù ù
A quiet hum came from the refrigerator in the kitchen.
worry: The physical problem is the one archivists worry about least.
some: an unspecified amount or number of something
Could you buy some bread on your way home?
journalists: people who write or report news for a living
Several journalists gathered outside the courthouse to cover the trial.
responded: The government responded to the criticism with a new policy.
called: named or referred to by a particular term
The recipe uses a fermented paste called miso for extra flavour.
solutions: ways of solving problems or dealing with difficult situations
The team brainstormed several solutions to the traffic problem.
serious: requiring careful thought or attention; not casual
He gave a serious answer instead of joking as usual.
attempts: She attempts the crossword every morning before breakfast.
address: the details of where a person lives or a place is located
She wrote her new address on the back of the envelope.
including: containing as part of a larger group; used to give an example
Several countries, including Vietnam, signed the new trade agreement.
fail: to not succeed at something attempted
Many new businesses fail within their first two years.
aim: a purpose or intention; a desired outcome
Her main aim this year is to finish the marathon under four hours.
replace: to put something new in the place of another
They had to replace the broken window before winter.
cheerful: showing or causing happiness and positivity
Her cheerful attitude made the long meeting easier to bear.
give: to hand over or provide something to someone
Please give the documents to the manager before noon.
complete: having all the necessary or appropriate parts; whole
The library keeps a complete collection of the author's early novels.
being: existing, or the fact of existing in a particular state
Being tired all week, she decided to cancel her weekend plans.
tried: past tense of try; made an attempt at something
It began to look incomplete when researchers tried the obvious thing and told people the truth.
actually: in fact; really, contrary to what might be expected
The film was actually shot in a different country than the story suggests.
works: This explains why rereading notes feels productive and works so poorly.
habits: things done regularly, almost without thinking
Good sleeping habits make a noticeable difference to concentration.
checking: the act of examining something to make sure it is correct
Checking the figures twice avoided an embarrassing mistake in the report.
once: immediately, without delay (used in the phrase 'at once')
The fire alarm made everyone leave the building at once.
twice: In a cold kitchen the dough may need twice that time to rise.
constantly: New apps are constantly being released to compete for users' attention.
reduces: makes something smaller or less in amount
Regular exercise reduces the risk of many chronic illnesses.
permanent: lasting or intended to last indefinitely; not temporary
After years of renting, they finally found a permanent home for their family.
emergency: a serious, unexpected situation requiring immediate action
Call this number only in a genuine emergency.
articles: pieces of writing published in a newspaper or magazine
The journal publishes new scientific articles every month.
explain: to make something clear by describing it in detail
Walking and reading a face were solved long before anyone could explain how.
causes: makes something happen; produces an effect
Poor drainage often causes flooding after heavy rain.
inform: to give someone facts or knowledge about something
cung cấp thông tin, thông báo
The manager will inform staff about the new schedule tomorrow.
breaking: separating something into pieces or parts
The enzyme works by breaking down large molecules into smaller ones.
alerts: warnings or notices about something requiring attention
Weather alerts were sent to every phone in the affected counties.
helps: assists; third person singular of help
A short walk after lunch helps digestion considerably.
ask: to put a question to someone or request something
Feel free to ask if you need help with the homework.
simple: easy to understand or do; not complicated
He gave a simple explanation that even a child could understand.
question: /ˈkwestʃən/
n
a sentence asked to get information or express doubt
câu hỏi, vấn đề
Nobody could answer the teacher's difficult question about gravity.
query
inquiry
issue
any: used to refer to one or some of a thing, no matter which
Do you have any questions before we begin the meeting?
alarming: The report revealed an alarming rise in river pollution levels.
becoming: The town is becoming a popular spot for young families.
critics: people who express disapproval or judge the faults of something
nhà phê bình, người chỉ trích
Critics praised the novel's honest portrayal of grief.
warn: to tell someone about a possible danger or problem
Some researchers warn against talking about a loneliness epidemic.
advice: guidance or recommendations offered about future action
Her grandmother's advice on saving money still guides her today.
like: similar to, or in the same way as
Her handwriting looks a lot like her mother's.
go: to move or travel from one place to another
We should go before the traffic gets worse.
too: The height of the band carries information too.
luxury: something expensive and not essential, giving great comfort
A quiet weekend away has become a rare luxury for parents.
everyone: Everyone who has measured it agrees on the shape of the answer.
farmer: a person who owns or manages a farm
The farmer rose before dawn to milk the cows.
watching: looking at something for a period of time
Somebody had to be watching, accountable to the users rather than a distant office.
storm: a period of very bad weather with strong winds and rain
A sudden storm forced the fishing boats back to shore.
forecast: a prediction of what will happen, especially the weather
The forecast predicts heavy rain for the whole weekend.
living: She is one of the few living witnesses to that event.
near: at a short distance from a place, time or state
They built their house near a small, quiet lake.
conflict: a serious disagreement or clash between opposing interests
The two managers had a conflict over how to spend the budget.
cannot: used to say that something is not possible or not allowed
Visitors cannot enter the site without prior written permission.
look: to direct one's eyes in order to see
Look both ways carefully before crossing the busy street.
away: to or at a distance from a place or person
The children ran away when they saw the dog.
protecting: The soldiers were protecting the border village from further attacks.
peace: a state of calm, quiet, and freedom from disturbance
She went for a long walk to find some peace after work.
polite: having good manners; respectful and considerate toward others
He gave a polite response even though he disagreed completely.
excuse: a reason given to justify or explain an action
cái cớ, lý do biện minh
The lending desk works as an excuse for the real conversation.
ignoring: deliberately paying no attention to something
He kept ignoring the phone calls from unknown numbers.
suffering: the experience of pain, distress or hardship
The charity works to reduce suffering caused by famine.
elsewhere: in, at, or to another place
If this shop can't help, try looking elsewhere in town.
limiting: restricting the amount, extent, or scope of something
The council discussed limiting traffic in the historic centre.
care: serious attention or caution applied to a task
Handle the antique vase with great care while moving it.
enough: as much or as many as needed
There was barely enough food to feed everyone at the table.
reserve: an amount of something kept for future use
The country keeps a large reserve of rice for emergencies.
matter: a subject or situation being considered or discussed
Choosing the right career is a matter that deserves careful thought.
goal: an aim or desired result that someone works towards
Her main goal this year is to save enough money to travel.
knowing: having information or understanding about something
Knowing when to stop working is an important skill for bakers.
proportion: a part or share of a whole, considered in relation to it
A large proportion of the budget is spent on staff salaries.
take: to get hold of, remove, or carry something
Please take a seat while you wait for the doctor.
dangers: possibilities of harm, injury, or loss
The guide warned hikers about the dangers of the steep trail.
seriously: in a way that shows careful thought; genuinely
Doctors are taking the new symptoms seriously.
while: It makes the city liveable while the wider problem is dealt with separately.
remembering: the act of bringing something back to mind
Remembering everyone's name at the party was hard.
slow: The traffic was slow because of the heavy rain.
unreported: not made known publicly; not covered by the news
Slow, unreported improvements are also part of the truth.
improvements: changes that make something better, plural
The team made several improvements to the design this year.
truth: the quality of being in accordance with fact; something that is true
On paper, the estimate is closer to the truth.
diet: the food that a person or animal usually eats
A balanced diet includes plenty of fruit and vegetables.
shaped: formed or made into a particular shape
The clay was shaped into a small bowl before drying.
balance: a state in which different things are of equal weight or importance
Finding a balance between work and rest is not always easy.
uncomfortable: causing or feeling physical or mental unease
It changes where the effort goes, towards the uncomfortable minutes spent trying to remember.
times: plural of time; particular occasions or periods
This is why recipes that give exact times are unreliable.
likely: It is likely that ticket prices will rise again next year.
leave: to go away from a place, or to allow something to remain

afraid: feeling fear or anxiety about something
She was afraid of speaking in front of such a large crowd.
